{"findings": [
{"file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts", "line": 8, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `z.string().toString()` as a computed key, so it never validates real token responses", "body": "`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `toString()` on a Zod object at module load. That yields a literal key such as \"[object Object]\", not a wildcard 'any numeric property'. The schema therefore requires a property literally named \"[object Object]\" to be a number, and no real token response has one. The second computed key on line 10 is just as broken. Whenever credential sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `safeParse` fails and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Every app routed through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (Google, Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) is broken in sync mode. The 'any numeric field is the expiry' rule needs something like `.passthrough().refine(...)`, not computed keys."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts", "line": 97, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed data", "body": "Before this change `key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the credential object. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`). `data: { key }` therefore stores `{ success, data: { ... } }` as the credential key. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, because `access_token`, `refresh_token` and the other fields are now nested under `data`. Every Google Calendar token refresh corrupts the stored credential, even with sync disabled. It should use `.data` from the parse result."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts", "line": 96, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "`prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService", "body": "The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but the file has no `import prisma from \"@calcom/prisma\"`. This fails type-check and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Because `getClient` runs from the constructor, every Salesforce calendar operation is affected."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts", "line": 75, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "Salesforce refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, runs on every instantiation and then uses the stale access token", "body": "The new block calls login.salesforce.com directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is not honoured for Salesforce. It also runs unconditionally, with no expiry check, so every service construction does a token refresh and a DB write. The `jsforce.Connection` that follows still uses `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token), not the one just fetched and persisted. The `response.statusText !== \"OK\"` check is fragile: statusText is empty on HTTP/2 responses, so a successful refresh would be treated as failure."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts", "line": 93, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "Credential id is passed to refreshOAuthTokens where a user id is expected", "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens(..., \"zoho-bigin\", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the `userId` argument. In sync mode this sends `calcomUserId=<credentialId>` to the self-hoster's endpoint, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or none. The credential's `userId` isn't available in `biginAuth`/`refreshAccessToken` as written, so it has to be threaded through. Teams credentials with a null `userId` should also skip sync, but a credential id is always truthy, so they can't."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts", "line": 15, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, but most callers expect a different shape", "body": "In sync mode the function returns the raw `fetch` Response. The non-sync callbacks return other shapes, and callers rely on them. Google reads `res?.data` (a gaxios response), so `token.access_token` throws and the error is swallowed, leaving the stale token. Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object, so it reads `.expiresIn` on a Response, gets NaN, and stores the Response as the credential key. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios), which is undefined on a Response and throws; the Bigin call is not wrapped in try/catch. The sync result needs to be normalised to the shape each caller expects, or each caller needs to parse the Response, and it needs to be exercised in tests."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts", "line": 8, "severity": "medium", "category": "security", "title": "Request to the credential-sync endpoint is unauthenticated and unchecked", "body": "The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. The response is also returned without checking `response.ok` or setting a timeout. A 4xx/5xx body then flows into the callers' parsing as if it were token data."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts", "line": 25, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "Placeholder refresh_token is injected unconditionally, including when sync is off", "body": "If the parsed data has no `refresh_token`, the literal string \"refresh_token\" is set, even without credential sync. Office365 Calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the existing credential, so a response lacking `refresh_token` replaces the real refresh token with the string \"refresh_token\". Later refreshes then fail permanently. The fallback should apply only in sync mode, and should not overwrite an existing token."},
{"file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts", "line": 88, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "Webex still uses the strict refreshed-token schema, so sync mode cannot succeed", "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens` was added for Webex, but the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `z.string().toString()` as a computed key, so it never validates real token responses
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `toString()` on a Zod object at module load. That yields a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a wildcard 'any numeric property'. The schema therefore requires a property literally named "[object Object]" to be a number, and no real token response has one. The second computed key on line 10 is just as broken. Whenever credential sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `safeParse` fails and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Every app routed through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (Google, Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) is broken in sync mode. The 'any numeric field is the expiry' rule needs something like `.passthrough().refine(...)`, not computed keys.

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed data
findings.body: Before this change `key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the credential object. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`). `data: { key }` therefore stores `{ success, data: { ... } }` as the credential key. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, because `access_token`, `refresh_token` and the other fields are now nested under `data`. Every Google Calendar token refresh corrupts the stored credential, even with sync disabled. It should use `.data` from the parse result.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This fails type-check and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Because `getClient` runs from the constructor, every Salesforce calendar operation is affected.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, runs on every instantiation and then uses the stale access token
findings.body: The new block calls login.salesforce.com directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is not honoured for Salesforce. It also runs unconditionally, with no expiry check, so every service construction does a token refresh and a DB write. The `jsforce.Connection` that follows still uses `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token), not the one just fetched and persisted. The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is fragile: statusText is empty on HTTP/2 responses, so a successful refresh would be treated as failure.

findings.title: Credential id is passed to refreshOAuthTokens where a user id is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the `userId` argument. In sync mode this sends `calcomUserId=<credentialId>` to the self-hoster's endpoint, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or none. The credential's `userId` isn't available in `biginAuth`/`refreshAccessToken` as written, so it has to be threaded through. Teams credentials with a null `userId` should also skip sync, but a credential id is always truthy, so they can't.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, but most callers expect a different shape
findings.body: In sync mode the function returns the raw `fetch` Response. The non-sync callbacks return other shapes, and callers rely on them. Google reads `res?.data` (a gaxios response), so `token.access_token` throws and the error is swallowed, leaving the stale token. Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object, so it reads `.expiresIn` on a Response, gets NaN, and stores the Response as the credential key. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios), which is undefined on a Response and throws; the Bigin call is not wrapped in try/catch. The sync result needs to be normalised to the shape each caller expects, or each caller needs to parse the Response, and it needs to be exercised in tests.

findings.title: Request to the credential-sync endpoint is unauthenticated and unchecked
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. There is no shared secret or signature, even though the inbound webhook requires one. Anyone who can reach that endpoint can request OAuth access tokens for any Cal.com user id. The response is also returned without checking `response.ok` or setting a timeout. A 4xx/5xx body then flows into the callers' parsing as if it were token data.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token is injected unconditionally, including when sync is off
findings.body: If the parsed data has no `refresh_token`, the literal string "refresh_token" is set, even without credential sync. Office365 Calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the existing credential, so a response lacking `refresh_token` replaces the real refresh token with the string "refresh_token". Later refreshes then fail permanently. The fallback should apply only in sync mode, and should not overwrite an existing token.

findings.title: Webex still uses the strict refreshed-token schema, so sync mode cannot succeed
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` was added for Webex, but the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. The schema requires a fixed `scope` literal, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A sync endpoint that returns only an access token and expiry fails with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Zoom was migrated to `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so the apps are handled inconsistently.

findings.title: Unhandled validation and decryption errors return 500; secret compared non-constant-time
findings.body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input. `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` also throw on a wrong key or malformed payload. None of these are caught, so the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a 400 and may leak stack information. The HTTP method is never checked. The webhook secret is compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. When updating an existing credential, `invalid` is not reset, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after a successful sync.

findings.title: Token-parse failure now throws and the diagnostic logging was dropped
findings.body: Previously a schema mismatch logged the zod error and the MS response and then continued. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', and the `console.error` with the zod error and MS response body was removed. This is a behaviour change, and the information needed to debug why a refresh failed is lost. The later `tokenResponse.success && ...` is now redundant.

findings.title: redirect_uri hard-coded in add.ts but still derived from appConfig.slug in callback.ts
findings.body: `add.ts` now builds the redirect URI from the literal 'zoho-bigin', while `callback.ts` still uses `appConfig.slug` for the token exchange. OAuth requires both redirect URIs to match exactly. This only works as long as the config slug equals 'zoho-bigin'. The change is unrelated to the feature and creates a silent coupling.

findings.title: No tests for the new webhook, token parsing or sync refresh path
findings.body: The PR adds a credential-writing webhook and changes the token-refresh path of about ten apps, and the PR checklist says no tests were added. The parsing and return-shape bugs elsewhere in this PR (the broken computed keys, the unwrapped safeParse result, the missing prisma import, the credentialId/userId mix-up) would all have been caught by even basic unit tests.
